validity.researcher_notes: This row (RouteAccuracy='very low (straight line/schematic)') is the short (LengthKnownKm=2.01) BWEC lateral, not Vector's mainline. The Blue Water Energy Center is independently documented (DTE's own commercial-operation announcement; nsenergybusiness.com project profile) as located in East China Township, St. Clair County, Michigan, receiving feed gas 'through a short, lateral pipeline connection' tapped off Vector's mainline -- entirely within Michigan, with no source placing any part of the BWEC lateral in Ontario. The flagged first-endpoint coordinate (42.775, -82.479) sits in the St. Clair River corridor essentially on top of the US-Canada boundary line itself, a few miles from Vector's own, well-documented mainline border crossing at St. Clair River M.P. 333.4 (Marysville, MI / Sombra, ON) -- so on a schematic/straight-line route (not a traced pipe centerline), a vertex meant to mark 'where this lateral ties into Vector's system' landing a fraction of a degree onto the Canadian side of that narrow river is far more consistent with drawing/boundary-snap imprecision than with BWEC's lateral genuinely crossing into Canada. This is a route-geometry question, not a row-attribute error, so no fill applies -- flagged for routes-repo geometry review per standing rule 8.
